Subject: Staged evaluation metrics -> reservation SLA & burst triggers

Hi Daniel —

Great talking earlier. Attached is a short staged MAP (staged_MAP_v1.pdf) that maps your POC milestones to a reservation ramp and the commercial breakpoints we'd need to finalize pricing. Key points up front:

- Evaluation checkpoints at weeks 2, 4, and 8 with concrete pass criteria (latency 90th ≤ 120ms, successful KV cache hit ≥ 85% on typical workload, 99.9% inference availability during test windows).
- Initial pilot footprint: 2x A100-80GB equiv (GPU pool sized to support 40 concurrent sessions at target seq lengths); reserve option starts at 4x for committed capacity.
- Pricing model: lower unit price for committed capacity (12/24 month tiers). Ramp discounts at the 4-week and 8-week milestones tied to signed addenda.
- Burst clause: on-demand burst up to 2x committed pool for up to 48 hours per calendar month; billing for burst usage at 1.6x committed unit price unless we agree to a capped burst-credits model.

Can you confirm: 1) the evaluation acceptance criteria look like what your engineering team expects, and 2) whether Procurement needs an alternate billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly)? I attached a short GPU profile and an early SOW redline for reference.

If that looks good I propose we lock the MAP this week and schedule a technical kickoff for next Monday (May 24).

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference

Sergio —

Thanks for the doc. A couple of clarifying questions before I share with our infra team:

1) Burst pricing: 1.6x sounds reasonable, but can you do a blended cap (e.g., first 24h at 1.2x then 1.6x thereafter) — our cost team prefers stair-stepped caps for predictable overage.
2) Term: we like the idea of starting with a 12-month commit but want a 6-month review to decide whether to extend to 24 months. Is a contractual breakpoint at month 6 feasible (price re-opener tied to usage tiers)?
3) If we fail a checkpoint (e.g., week 4 latency target not met), what happens to the commit — do we pause the reserve ramp until fixes are deployed, or proceed with a reduced commitment?

Also looped in Procurement to confirm billing cadence.

Team —

We can accommodate Acme's requests with these guardrails (pricing summary below). I'll drop the exact language into the SOW redline.

Pricing (high level):
- Commit tiers: 4-unit reserve (baseline) — $40k/mo (12-month) | 24-month = $36k/mo (6% effective discount).
- Ramp discounts: upon passing week-4 checkpoint, incremental units added to commit receive a 10% introductory discount for first 3 months; upon week-8 pass the discount becomes permanent for those units.
- Burst: stair-stepped cap as requested — first 24h at 1.2x, thereafter 1.6x up to 2x capacity. For large sustained bursts (>72h) we require a notice + Ops plan; sustained bursts billed at 2.2x.
- 6-month review: include a contractual re-opener tied to usage band thresholds (under 60% utilization → option to downscale with 60-day notice, over 95% sustained → option to increase committed units at pre-agreed uplift). Pricing re-opener limited to index-linked adjustment (CPU/GPU price index +2%) to avoid wide swings.

Evaluation failures: default operational route is to pause additions to committed ramp until remediation is complete (we'll keep pilot capacity at the initial footprint). If the failure is due to Redwood service degradation (we miss SLOs), we offer pro-rated credits and the option for Acme to defer ramp without penalty. If it is due to customer workload changes, we work through a remediation plan and may offer a one-time extension of the evaluation window.

Marissa — please add legal wording for the 6-month review, the burst stair-step, and the remediation/credit fallback. Ben — confirm we can commit to the discount choreography above.

—Laura

Daniel —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We can proceed with the blended burst cap and a 6-month contractual review. Key updates for your team:

- Burst: first 24 hours billed at 1.2x the committed unit price, thereafter 1.6x for up to 48 additional hours (72h total) per event; sustained >72h requires planning and billed at 2.2x. We'll include a one-time 24-hour courtesy burst credit for onboarding week.
- Term & breakpoint: 12-month initial commitment with a formal 6-month review clause. Re-opener is limited to the usage bands Laura outlined and an index-linked adjustment (GPU price index +2%).
- Checkpoints & failure behavior: if a checkpoint is missed due to Redwood service shortfall, Acme receives pro-rated service credits and we pause ramp additions until the SLOs are restored. If the checkpoint fails because of workload mismatch, we'll jointly agree a remediation plan and allow a single 2-week extension of the evaluation window.

Next steps: 1) I'm scheduling a 30-min technical kickoff for Mon May 24 at 10am PT (invite to follow). 2) I'll upload the SOW redline (SOW_terms_redline.docx) to the HubSpot deal and share the link. If Procurement prefers monthly billing we'll reflect that in the SOW; otherwise default is quarterly invoicing.

If that aligns I'm happy to mark the MAP as agreed and circulate the SOW for signature.

Best —
